media:group.media:title: Greening the Grey: Increasing #biodiversity in #coastaldefences (short) #geography #sustainability
media:group.media:description:
🌊 What if flood defences could protect coastlines and create habitats for marine life at the same time?
Professor Larissa Naylor worked together with industry to develop concrete Ecotiles and rock pools that create habitats for marine life, increasing biodiversity along engineered coastlines.
Industry partner Poundfield Precast produced three rock pools that were installed as part of an Environment Agency flood defence scheme on Canvey Island. The rock pools are already delivering results, with seaweeds, shrimps and other marine species colonising the structures just 2.5 years after installation.
The Ecotiles and rock pools are now available from Poundfield Precast for use in future coastal defence projects.
Find out more at: https://www.gla.ac.uk/colleges/scienceengineering/research/epsrciaa/casestudies/greeningthegrey/
Professor Naylor's project, ‘Greening the Grey’, was supported by the EPSRC Impact Acceleration Account at the University of Glasgow.
#flooding #researchimpact #universityofglasgow

entry.title: How has the world changed over the past 575 years?

media:group.media:title: How has the world changed over the past 575 years?
media:group.media:description:
Since opening our doors in 1451, we've not only witnessed change, we've helped shape it!
From expanding our understanding of what it means to be human, to pioneering medical advances, influencing economics and social justice, and driving innovations that have transformed how we live, generations of UofG world changers have left their mark.
As we celebrate our 575th Anniversary Year, we look back at the discoveries, ideas and breakthroughs that have changed lives and shaped the world, while looking ahead to the future that today's world-changers are helping to shape.
Discover more: glasgow.ac.uk/explore/575/researchandimpact/
